subject: Geography
central_question: How does atmospheric water move through humidity, evaporation, condensation, clouds and precipitation to create weather and rainfall patterns?
in_scope_units: Water vapour, humidity, saturation and dew point
banned_topics: Detailed atmospheric circulation and cyclone formation from Chapter 9
Hydrological cycle and ocean-floor relief from Chapter 12

known_pitfalls.claim: Relative humidity is the actual mass of vapour in a unit volume.
known_pitfalls.correction: That is absolute humidity; relative humidity compares present moisture with full capacity at the same temperature.

known_pitfalls.claim: Fog and mist are unrelated to clouds.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes fog as a cloud at or near the ground and both as condensation around particles.

known_pitfalls.claim: The leeward side receives more orographic rain.
known_pitfalls.correction: Windward slopes receive more; leeward descending air creates a rain-shadow area.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 2(iv): explain cloud formation and classification
NCERT Exercise 3(ii): describe condensation forms, dew and frost
NCERT Exercise 3(i): discuss world precipitation distribution
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 and Project Work on tracking extreme rainfall reports.
